871b49f0.task: Which programming language is ranked most popular in the latest Stack Overflow developer survey, and who originally created it?
871b49f0.label: fail
871b49f0.notes: Verified via web search: the real 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey reports JavaScript as still the most-used language (66%). Python's actual 2025 headline was fastest-growing usage (+7 points) and most-desired-to-learn-next -- a different metric entirely from 'most popular.' The agent found the correct, current survey (the date fix worked) but misread/conflated two different stats into the wrong headline conclusion. This is a more advanced failure than simple staleness: the retrieval was correct, the synthesis was not.

d52c7e87.task: Who is the CEO of the parent company of the airline with the most domestic routes in the United States?
d52c7e87.label: fail
d52c7e87.notes: Technically converged on an answer this time (Southwest Airlines / Bob Jordan, both individually correct facts), so this would look like a pass in isolation. Labeling as fail because: the previous batch's run of the exact same question, with no code changes, confidently answered American Airlines / Robert Isom instead. Both chains are internally correct but the underlying ranking premise is genuinely contested, and the agent never acknowledges that -- it just picks an answer with full confidence each time, and which answer it picks isn't stable across runs. This is the most important finding so far: only visible by running the same question multiple times, not catchable from a single trace.
